s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and fungal forms
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient has well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
No systemic complaints
No history of high-risk behavior for HIV
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and other cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral ulceration with granulomatous inflammation
salient_findings: Ulcer with clean base and irregular, elevated margins
Histopathological findings of dense diffuse infiltrate with lymphocytes, histiocytes, and fungal forms
key_facts: 40-year-old man from eastern India
Presented with a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue for 4 months
Lesion started as a small painless mass on the right lateral aspect of the tongue
No history of trauma or tongue bite preceding the lesion
Patient has well-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
No systemic complaints
No history of high-risk behavior for HIV
Single well-defined ulcer measuring 2 × 2 cm on the right lateral aspect of tongue
Histopathological examination showed dense diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and other cells
Intracellular yeasts with a surrounding halo were found in histiocytes
Special stains highlighted fungal forms
Fungal culture on Sabouraud dextrose agar was negative
HIV-1 and HIV-2 serologic testing were negative

raw.rationale: The presence of a nonhealing ulcer on the tongue, histopathological findings of a dense diffuse infiltrate with intracellular yeasts and giant cells, and the patient's origin from eastern India, a region with a high prevalence of tuberculosis, support this diagnosis. Although fungal culture was negative, the clinical and histopathological features are more consistent with tuberculosis, especially given the lack of evidence for other conditions.

rejected.label: tuberculosis
rejected.why: Too broad, as the specific location of the tuberculosis is on the tongue

rejected.label: wound
rejected.why: Does not explain the underlying cause of the ulcer

rejected.label: ulcer
rejected.why: Too general, as it does not specify the etiology

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and non-caseating granulomas, which are not described in this case
